metadata.research_goal: Synthesize credible-source guidance for cycling endurance and power programming into backend-ready records for zones, FTP/threshold, HR/RPE, cadence, block design, progression, tapering, indoor trainer use, recovery, intensity distribution, and fueling.
metadata.write_scope: single draft file for endurance and power programming only
metadata.synthesis_note: Records prioritize planning rules, progression gates, session-quality signals, and warning flags rather than broad cycling tips.

key_concepts.concept: Cycling intensity should be triangulated from power, HR, RPE, cadence, terrain, duration, and recovery response.
key_concepts.backend_use: Do not require power data to create plans, but when power exists use it as the primary external-load target and cross-check against HR/RPE drift.

key_concepts.concept: FTP or threshold power is a useful anchor for endurance cycling zones because it reflects sustainable aerobic power more directly than maximal power.
key_concepts.backend_use: Power-zone plans should store zones relative to FTP/threshold and retest only when performance signals make current zones stale.

key_concepts.concept: Heart rate is valuable but delayed and sensitive to fatigue, heat, nerves, hydration, and cardiac drift.
key_concepts.backend_use: For short intervals and stochastic rides, use HR mainly for post-session interpretation; for steady endurance and threshold work, pair HR with power or RPE.

key_concepts.concept: RPE is essential when FTP or HR zones are missing and remains useful as a fatigue and execution-quality signal even with sensors.
key_concepts.backend_use: Every workout target should have an RPE fallback so beginner and low-equipment cyclists can train safely.

key_concepts.concept: There is no universal cadence target; optimal cadence shifts with intensity, power demand, fatigue, terrain, gearing, and rider skill.
key_concepts.backend_use: Program cadence ranges and drills as skill/neuromuscular tools, not as mandatory one-size-fits-all RPM rules.

key_concepts.concept: Endurance riding at conversational to purposeful low intensity builds the base that supports harder tempo, threshold, VO2, sprint, and race efforts.
key_concepts.backend_use: Plans should protect enough low-intensity volume even when athletes request more intervals or races.

key_concepts.concept: A ride average can hide poor execution; time in target zone and interval repeat quality matter more than average speed or average HR.
key_concepts.backend_use: Session assessment should store target-compliance metrics such as time in zone, power fade, HR drift, and RPE mismatch.

key_concepts.concept: Cycling plans commonly use several progressive build weeks followed by lower-load recovery to convert training stress into adaptation.
key_concepts.backend_use: Block generator should default to 2-3 build weeks plus 1 recovery week, with level-specific adjustments.

key_concepts.concept: Indoor training is efficient because it removes traffic, route, weather, and coasting constraints and allows exact intensity-duration control.
key_concepts.backend_use: Use indoor trainer options for short high-quality intervals, winter blocks, time-crunched users, and controlled assessments.

key_concepts.concept: Fueling and hydration determine whether prescribed endurance and intensity work can be executed and recovered from.
key_concepts.backend_use: Session prescriptions longer than 60 minutes or involving threshold/VO2/sprint density should include carbohydrate and hydration prompts.

key_concepts.concept: A cyclist's performance profile includes short sprint power, anaerobic capacity, 4-5 minute aerobic power, threshold power, durability, and skill/aerodynamics.
key_concepts.backend_use: Assessment records should avoid classifying riders from FTP alone; include sprint, short aerobic, endurance durability, and discipline context.

key_concepts.concept: Polarized, pyramidal, threshold, and high-volume models are tools; their usefulness depends on rider level, block phase, event, available time, and recovery capacity.
key_concepts.backend_use: Plan templates should choose intensity distribution by phase and context instead of hard-coding a universal 80/20 rule.

fields.z3_tempo: about 76-90% FTP; muscular endurance and sustained pace
fields.z4_threshold: about 91-105% FTP; sustained hard work, often 10-30 minute repeats
fields.z6_anaerobic: above 120% FTP; 30 second to 3 minute efforts
fields.z7_neuromuscular: maximal sprint power; not percentage-FTP based

technical_models.programming_use: Primary power target model when FTP exists; add RPE and HR descriptions to each zone.

fields.active_recovery: very easy, no burning or fatigue
fields.endurance: steady all-day pace and long-ride base
fields.tempo: purposeful intensive endurance with short-sentence conversation
fields.threshold: near sustainable red-line; novices must build toward it
fields.vo2max: very hard 3-8 minute efforts with heavy breathing
fields.anaerobic: maximal sprint efforts where HR lags too much to prescribe

technical_models.programming_use: Use for HR-based plans and for explaining RPE/power targets in human terms.

fields.rpe_4: all-day sustainable ride with full conversation
fields.rpe_8: few-minute hard effort with one-word communication

technical_models.programming_use: Attach to all no-sensor sessions and as a compliance check for power/HR sessions.

fields.normalized_power: estimates physiological cost of variable cycling power
fields.intensity_factor: normalized power divided by FTP; compares relative session intensity
fields.average_power_warning: can understate stochastic race or criterium load
fields.event_inference: hard 1-hour race normalized power can help estimate threshold when formal testing is absent

technical_models.programming_use: Use NP/IF to classify outdoor stochastic rides, race simulations, and group rides that do not match steady-zone targets.

fields.default_sequence: 2-3 progressive build weeks followed by one reduced-load week
fields.intermediate_example: three priority rides per week: two midweek structured rides plus one weekend ride
fields.optional_volume_rule: bonus sessions are added only when they do not reduce key-session quality
fields.recovery_logic: adaptation is realized through recovery, not continual weekly escalation

technical_models.programming_use: Macro-plan and 4-week block generator default for non-novice cyclists.

fields.base_phase: mostly low intensity with long-ride durability and limited tempo
fields.threshold_build: controlled tempo/sweet-spot/threshold intervals with protected low-intensity rides
fields.vo2_block: small number of high-quality VO2 sessions plus low-intensity support
fields.polarized_option: large low-intensity share plus limited high-intensity work for well-trained riders
fields.pyramidal_option: low-intensity base, moderate tempo exposure, and smaller high-intensity dose for many real-world riders
fields.avoidance: do not let most rides drift into unplanned moderate fatigue

technical_models.programming_use: Select distribution based on level, event demands, available time, and recovery state.

fields.endurance_default: self-selected efficient cadence with comfort and no joint stress
fields.low_cadence_force: short controlled force work only for prepared riders and symptom-free knees
fields.high_cadence_leg_speed: low-load drills to improve coordination and cadence range
fields.sprint_cadence: maximal efforts depend on gear, force, and velocity; compare to prior similar efforts
fields.assessment: cadence target is acceptable when power, RPE, HR, and pain response stay within intent

technical_models.programming_use: Cadence drill planner and warning rules for big-gear grinding.

fields.threshold: 20-60 minute field estimate or modeled FTP
fields.durability: power or HR drift after long endurance load
fields.repeatability: ability to reproduce intervals or sprints late in a ride

technical_models.programming_use: Classify rider strengths, select sprint/VO2/threshold focus, and avoid overusing FTP as the only assessment.

fields.best_uses: interval precision, short sessions, winter/time-crunched blocks, repeatable testing
fields.data_quality: warm up trainer and calibrate; maintain tire pressure for wheel-on trainers
fields.erg_mode_use: use ERG for precise dose, but also practice self-pacing near race season
fields.limitations: indoor riding does not train bike handling, group skills, descending, or outdoor pacing variability

technical_models.programming_use: Convert outdoor workouts to trainer-safe versions and flag handling-skill deficits before events.

fields.goal: reduce accumulated fatigue while preserving fitness and neuromuscular sharpness
fields.volume: reduce total load more than intensity
fields.intensity: maintain short event-specific efforts if recovery permits
fields.duration: commonly 1-2 weeks for A events, individualized by fatigue depth, event duration, and rider level
fields.novelty_rule: avoid new fit, equipment, fueling, and interval formats near competition

technical_models.programming_use: A-event peak planning and final 7-14 day workout adjustment.

fields.daily_carbohydrate: scale to upcoming training load and intensity
fields.pre_session: for exercise over 60 minutes, plan carbohydrate 1-4 g/kg in the 1-4 hours before when appropriate
fields.during_session: 30-90 g carbohydrate per hour for rides over 60 minutes, scaled by duration and intensity
fields.high_intake: use glucose-fructose or mixed saccharide approaches for higher hourly carbohydrate targets
fields.post_session: rapid carbohydrate recovery is most important after exhaustive work or when another key session follows soon

technical_models.programming_use: Attach fueling prompts and underfueling warnings to long rides, threshold blocks, VO2 blocks, and multi-session days.

tactical_rules.rule: If the goal is recovery or low-intensity endurance, cap intensity with conversation-level RPE and avoid chasing speed, segments, or group surges.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Downgrade plan compliance when easy rides become tempo or threshold by HR/RPE/power.

tactical_rules.rule: Optional rides, bonus sessions, cross-training, and group rides are allowed only if they do not compromise the week's key sessions.
tactical_rules.backend_action: If key-session quality drops, remove optional volume before reducing the targeted workout.

tactical_rules.rule: Avoid stacking threshold intervals, VO2 intervals, sprints, race-like group rides, long rides, and heavy lower-body strength in the same short window.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Flag excessive high-intensity density and insert recovery or low-intensity endurance.

tactical_rules.rule: When power target and RPE sharply disagree, treat the session as a monitoring problem rather than blindly forcing watts.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Prompt checks for fatigue, heat, calibration, illness, fueling, and FTP staleness.

tactical_rules.rule: Do not prescribe anaerobic or neuromuscular sprint targets by HR because HR response lags behind the effort.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Use power, cadence/gear, duration, maximal intent, full recovery, and prior comparable sprint values.

tactical_rules.rule: Sprint and neuromuscular sessions should prioritize maximal quality and long rests rather than fatigue accumulation.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Place sprint work early in the ride or after full recovery; stop if power, form, or coordination deteriorates.

tactical_rules.rule: For riders with weak endurance base or saddle tolerance, progress long easy rides before adding multiple weekly hard sessions.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Gate threshold/VO2 blocks behind stable weekly riding, long-ride tolerance, and no pain spikes.

tactical_rules.rule: A events receive event-specific preparation and taper; B events receive short freshness; C events are training opportunities.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Ask event priority before tapering or disrupting a productive block.

tactical_rules.rule: Frequent racing can crowd out targeted training and low-intensity base, even when total ride hours appear high.
tactical_rules.backend_action: If schedule becomes race-recover-race, reduce event count or classify some events as C workouts.

tactical_rules.rule: Before FTP tests or precise indoor intervals, warm up and calibrate the trainer, and control wheel-on tire pressure.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Invalidate or annotate power-test results if calibration or setup is uncertain.

tactical_rules.rule: ERG mode is useful for exact dose but riders also need self-paced execution for outdoor racing, climbing, time trials, and group variability.
tactical_rules.backend_action: Near events, convert some controlled intervals to self-paced power/RPE targets.

tactical_rules.rule: Do not judge a failed threshold, VO2, or long endurance session without checking carbohydrate and hydration execution.
tactical_rules.backend_action: When power fades early or RPE spikes, log fueling quality before increasing training load or lowering FTP.

physical_demands.demand: High aerobic base and endurance durability for long rides, repeat training weeks, and support of all higher-intensity work.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Protect weekly low-intensity ride time and long-ride progression.

physical_demands.demand: Sustainable threshold power for climbs, time trials, hard group rides, breakaways, and endurance event red-line control.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Introduce tempo and threshold blocks only after basic endurance and recovery capacity are stable.

physical_demands.demand: VO2max and severe-domain power for 3-8 minute climbs, bridges, MTB surges, break initiation, and race selection moments.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Use limited, high-quality VO2 work with recovery; do not stack with other hard days.

physical_demands.demand: Short hard repeatability for attacks, criterium exits, punchy climbs, track efforts, cyclocross accelerations, and MTB bursts.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Program short intervals separately from pure sprints and threshold work.

physical_demands.demand: Very short maximal power and rate of force development for sprint finishes, standing starts, BMX, and track sprint contexts.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Use low-volume maximal efforts, long rests, and prior-best comparison instead of FTP percentages.

physical_demands.demand: Ability to produce power across cadence ranges as terrain, gears, fixed-gear constraints, fatigue, and event demands change.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Include low-stress leg-speed drills and controlled force work when appropriate.

physical_demands.demand: Muscular endurance for tempo, sweet spot, climbs, headwinds, and prolonged seated output.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Develop with tempo and sub-threshold blocks after basic base; monitor knee/back response.

physical_demands.demand: Ability to absorb hard sessions, long rides, and progressive blocks without accumulating non-functional fatigue.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Use recovery weeks, rest days, and subjective readiness signals as plan inputs.

physical_demands.demand: Gut and behavior tolerance for carbohydrate and fluid intake during long and high-quality rides.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Train fueling during long rides and race simulations before event day.

physical_demands.demand: Postural tolerance for sustained power indoors/outdoors, aero positions, climbing, and long rides.
physical_demands.programming_implication: Long-ride and trainer duration should progress with saddle, back, neck, and hand response.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Underfueling can cause premature power fade, high RPE, poor recovery, illness susceptibility, and low energy availability risk.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Check fueling before labeling a rider undertrained or increasing interval dose.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Too many races or race-like group rides can prevent targeted adaptation and erode aerobic base.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Detect weeks dominated by racing and recovery with little structured endurance or targeted work.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Too much VO2, anaerobic, sprint, and threshold work can outpace recovery and reduce quality.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Limit hard sessions per week based on level and recent fatigue; separate high-demand days.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Continual weekly load increases can create plateaus, non-recovery, poor sleep, low motivation, and illness risk.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: If warning signs appear, insert reduced-load week or season break rather than escalating training.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Excessive low-cadence high-torque riding can overload knees, calves, Achilles, and low back, especially in beginners or fit issues.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Regress big-gear work when knee or tendon symptoms occur and review cadence, gearing, saddle, and cleats.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: HR drift, lag, heat, fatigue, and nerves can mislead pacing and post-session judgment.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Use HR with RPE, power, environment, and hydration context instead of single-metric decisions.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Uncalibrated trainers, temperature shifts, and wheel-on tire-pressure changes can corrupt power targets and tests.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Flag suspicious power changes when setup or calibration changed.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Indoor-only blocks can preserve fitness but fail to maintain outdoor handling, group riding, and real-world pacing skills.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Before outdoor events, add outdoor rides and skill exposure instead of only trainer workouts.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: New equipment, bike fit, fueling, or unfamiliar interval formats near competition can undermine performance.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Freeze novelty during taper except for urgent safety fixes.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Aggressive carbohydrate intake without gut training or mixed-saccharide tolerance can cause GI symptoms and session failure.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Build fueling practice progressively and individualize high-carbohydrate targets.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Masters riders may need more recovery timing and careful strength/intensity integration because recovery needs can change with age.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Use readiness and quality markers to decide whether to repeat, hold, or progress hard sessions.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: Beginners without base, saddle tolerance, handling confidence, or recovery habits can be overloaded by threshold or VO2 blocks.
injury_or_load_risks.planning_warning: Gate high-intensity blocks behind ride frequency, endurance tolerance, and symptom-free easy riding.

training_implications.implication: Beginner cycling plans should start with easy ride habit, cadence awareness, comfort, fueling basics, and no pain spikes before structured FTP or VO2 work.
training_implications.backend_rule: Hold beginners in foundation/base blocks until they complete consistent easy rides and one longer ride without symptom flare.

training_implications.implication: Intermediate structured plans assume regular riding, usually three or more rides per week or readiness for interval-style workouts.
training_implications.backend_rule: If the rider cannot ride 2 hours or lacks recent ride frequency, select base or foundation instead of indoor intensity plan.

training_implications.implication: Long rides should be mostly endurance intensity early in plans and progress by duration only when fueling, comfort, and next-day response are acceptable.
training_implications.backend_rule: Increase long-ride duration conservatively and deload when saddle, knee, back, neck, hand, sleep, or fatigue signals worsen.

training_implications.implication: Threshold/FTP build blocks should concentrate time near threshold for a few weeks, usually with limited weekly interval sessions and low-intensity support.
training_implications.backend_rule: Use 2-3 threshold or related interval sessions per week only for prepared riders, and reduce if quality drops.

training_implications.implication: VO2 blocks should use short hard intervals with enough recovery and should not be added merely because the rider wants hard workouts.
training_implications.backend_rule: Require base, recent threshold tolerance, and stable recovery before VO2 progression.

training_implications.implication: Sprint blocks need fresh neuromuscular work, long rests, and comparison to prior similar efforts rather than percentage-FTP prescriptions.
training_implications.backend_rule: Stop sprint work when peak power falls materially, form degrades, or pain appears.

training_implications.implication: Cadence drills can be placed in easy or moderate rides to widen usable cadence range without compromising power targets.
training_implications.backend_rule: Do not place cadence drills inside key threshold/VO2 sets unless cadence is the main session objective.

training_implications.implication: Recovery rides should be very easy, short enough to improve circulation and loosen legs, and not used to add hidden training stress.
training_implications.backend_rule: If RPE or HR is elevated at recovery power, convert to rest or shorter spin.

training_implications.implication: Indoor sessions are ideal for precise intervals, but indoor-only programming needs outdoor handling and real-world pacing before events.
training_implications.backend_rule: Pair indoor intensity blocks with outdoor skill/route exposure when an outdoor event is on the calendar.

training_implications.implication: FTP testing should be done when rested, fueled, and with reliable power setup; recent race NP or modeled data can help estimate threshold but must be contextualized.
training_implications.backend_rule: Schedule tests after easier days and require calibration notes for trainer-based tests.

training_implications.implication: A-event taper should reduce volume while retaining enough intensity to preserve feel and fitness; B events need less taper and C events may be trained through.
training_implications.backend_rule: Ask event priority and fatigue status before assigning taper length.

training_implications.implication: A rider's intensity distribution should change across base, build, specificity, taper, and competition phases.
training_implications.backend_rule: Use polarized, pyramidal, threshold, or mixed distributions as phase tools, not identity labels.

training_implications.implication: Rides over 60 minutes and key hard sessions need explicit carbohydrate and fluid planning because poor fueling can mimic poor fitness.
training_implications.backend_rule: Add fueling tasks to workout records and collect post-session fueling compliance.

training_implications.implication: Training zones should be updated when repeated sessions are too easy/hard, HR/RPE no longer matches power, or recent testing/racing shows durable change.
training_implications.backend_rule: Trigger zone review after repeated interval overperformance, repeated underperformance, or a new validated power profile.

training_implications.implication: Plateau, poor sleep, low motivation, illness susceptibility, and non-recovery are reasons to reduce load before performance falls further.
training_implications.backend_rule: If two or more fatigue flags persist, replace hard sessions with rest/recovery and review fueling/sleep/load.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling intensity anchor hierarchy
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Use power when available, HR for internal load, RPE for all riders, cadence for movement quality, and recovery response for progression decisions.

backend_records_to_create.name: FTP-relative power zone table

backend_records_to_create.name: HR zone caveats and drift handling
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Store HR lag/drift/heat/fatigue caveats and rules for interpreting HR mismatches after workouts.

backend_records_to_create.name: RPE fallback for no-sensor rides

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling threshold or FTP build block

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling sprint and neuromuscular block

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling indoor time-efficient block
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Three ride weekly pattern with precise indoor intervals, quality-and-recovery emphasis, calibration reminders, and outdoor handling add-ons near events.

backend_records_to_create.name: Build-recovery week sequencer
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Default 2-3 build weeks then one recovery week; hold or deload early if fatigue flags persist.

backend_records_to_create.name: Optional volume quality gate
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Bonus rides are allowed only when key workout quality and recovery remain intact.

backend_records_to_create.name: A/B/C event priority and taper logic

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling excessive intensity density flag
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Flag weeks combining multiple threshold/VO2/sprint/race/long-ride/heavy-gym stressors without recovery.

backend_records_to_create.name: Underfueling session-quality flag
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: When power fades or RPE spikes, check carbohydrate, hydration, sleep, and heat before changing fitness assumptions.

backend_records_to_create.name: Big-gear low-cadence pain regression
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: If knee/calf/Achilles/back symptoms appear, remove high-torque cadence work and review gearing, cadence, fit, and recent load.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling power profile assessment
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Assess 6-second sprint, 30-second anaerobic power, 4-5 minute aerobic power, FTP/threshold, and durability instead of FTP alone.

backend_records_to_create.name: Endurance durability assessment
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Track HR drift, power fade, RPE rise, fueling compliance, and symptom response during long endurance rides.

backend_records_to_create.name: Indoor trainer calibration rule
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Warm up trainer, calibrate before tests/key workouts, and control tire pressure for wheel-on trainers.

backend_records_to_create.name: ERG mode transfer rule
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Use ERG for exact dose early or indoors, then add self-paced intervals near event specificity.

backend_records_to_create.name: Fuel for the work required
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Scale carbohydrate and hydration guidance by session duration, intensity, upcoming sessions, and gut tolerance.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cadence drill placement
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Place cadence drills in easy/moderate rides; keep them low stakes and stop when form or target compliance degrades.

backend_records_to_create.name: Sprint session stop rule
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: End sprint work when power drops, cadence control worsens, coordination declines, or pain appears.

backend_records_to_create.name: Training intensity distribution chooser
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Choose polarized, pyramidal, threshold, or mixed distribution by rider level, phase, event demands, available time, and recovery signals.

backend_records_to_create.name: Beginner to structured cycling readiness
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Progress when rider completes consistent easy rides, handles a longer endurance ride, understands RPE/cadence, fuels basic rides, and reports no pain spikes.

backend_records_to_create.name: Structured intensity hold rule
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Hold or regress when intervals repeatedly fail, HR/RPE is abnormal, sleep/motivation declines, illness appears, or fueling is inadequate.

backend_records_to_create.name: Over-racing guardrail
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Limit events that disrupt targeted blocks; classify races as A/B/C and preserve base training.

backend_records_to_create.name: Taper novelty freeze
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: During final A-event taper, avoid new equipment, fit, fueling, and unfamiliar workouts except urgent safety changes.
